extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to the Annals of Applied Statistics (AOAS)
extracted.subtask_description: Journal-specific submission and author guidelines for manuscripts to the Annals of Applied Statistics, covering scope/fit, writing and style expectations, submission format, supplementary materials, length, and editorial handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate paper scope
rubrics_metrics.description: We hope to publish papers that have substantive applied origins and involve relevant datasets, while also being of interest beyond the specific application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers that include innovative methodology brought to bear on scientific/policy questions and relevant data are especially welcome. Typically, a paper will be framed around one or more unresolved applied problems, where data are introduced to help address them. Data analyses should go well beyond numerical illustrations of calculations of proposed new methodology, with particular emphasis put on comparative analyses and substantive findings. Submissions without methodological innovation will be considered if the topic is of exceptionally broad interest, the application is groundbreaking, and the statistical methods used are state of the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgements should be limited to referencing: (a) named individuals who have contributed to the research by providing tangible inputs such as ideas, feedback, or code, (b) possibly-anonymous individuals who have served in the paper’s evaluation via the refereeing and editorial process, (c) organizations that provided funding, and/or (d) scientific institutions or meetings where the research was conducted or facilitated, if other than the home institution of an author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended readership and writing clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: AOAS is intended to be read by all professional statisticians, as well as by other scientists who are interested in particular areas of statistical application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is important for the abstract and introduction to say What scientific/policy question(s) the paper addresses, Why the topic is of interest, and How the data analyses will address these questions, in as non-technical a manner as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference citation format (name/year)
rubrics_metrics.description: References should be in the name/year format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initial reference in each section should be full, e.g., Smith, Jones, and Roberts (1992), using “et al.” for more than three authors; subsequent references can be abbreviated, e.g., Smith et al. (1992).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of IMS LaTeX template and citation settings
rubrics_metrics.description: We encourage use of the IMS LaTeX template when preparing your manuscript. The default setting is for numbered citations and references. To get the name-year format, change the line \RequirePackage[numbers]{natbib} to \RequirePackage{natbib} i.e., delete [numbers].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Template will set proper margins and font; sample.pdf and sample.tex files assist in preparation of a camera-ready paper in LaTeX. Please do not use any packages or commands that affect the layout or formatting of your document. See the LaTeX support page for IMS publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes are allowed, but should not be overused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may use British or American spelling, as they prefer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Most published papers will not exceed 20 pages (about 500 words per page, with figures typically taking 1/3 page and displayed equations 30 words each).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anything longer will require unusually compelling subject matter to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraged submission of data, code, and supporting material
rubrics_metrics.description: We strongly encourage submission of data sets, computer algorithms and supporting material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attached documents are allowed and strongly encouraged for data sets, algorithms etc. This can help the editors and referees in the review process. These supplementary materials will be archived along with the electronic versions of accepted papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary programs: self-contained and standard platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs should be self-contained and run on standard platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach program files as supplementary material so referees and editors can run them; ensure they are documented and runnable on common systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be submitted electronically via the Electronic Journal Management System (EJMS). Manuscripts must be submitted in pdf form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-time users must register (only required once). On the submission form you may suggest an area for assignment, but the editors may change it. Attached documents are allowed for supplements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archive and data availability / privacy considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: AOAS strongly encourages authors to make the data used in papers available for others to analyze, in keeping with the principle that scientific results need to be replicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If full public access is not possible due to confidentiality, privacy-protected extracts without identifiers may be sharable, or access can be arranged via special licensing or agreements. For material important to the paper but extensive or secondary, authors are encouraged to use web-based supplementary files (data sets, software, derivations, algorithms). Such supplements will be included in the review process and, when an article is accepted, will be permanently posted with the electronic version of the journal at Project Euclid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript handling and editorial decision process
rubrics_metrics.description: Your paper will be screened by the Editor-In-Chief and if appropriate it will be assigned to an Area Editor with relevant substantive and methodological expertise (you get to suggest an area on the submission form, but we may change the assignment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Area Editor has full control of your paper after assignment, including final decisions concerning publication. All further correspondence concerning the paper will be with the Area Editor.
